q: Which type should hold money amounts?
why: decimal stores base-10 digits exactly, so 0.1 + 0.2 is exactly 0.3. double works in base 2 and rounds.

q: What does this print?
why: 0.1 and 0.2 can't be stored exactly as double, so their sum is 0.30000000000000004.

q: What does this print?
why: The m suffix makes decimal literals; decimal adds them exactly.

q: What does this print?
why: unchecked lets the int wrap around to int.MinValue silently. It is also the default when you write neither keyword.

q: What does checked(int.MaxValue + someOne) do at run time when it overflows?
why: checked turns a silent wrap-around into a loud OverflowException.

q: Fill in the suffix that makes this a decimal literal.
why: m (or M) marks a decimal literal. Without it, 19.99 is a double and won't convert implicitly.

q: Which method reads a number from text without throwing on bad input?
why: TryParse returns false for bad input and gives the number through an out parameter.

q: Complete the safe parse.
why: int.TryParse(text, out int number) returns true only when the text is a valid int.

q: DateOnly stores a calendar date without a time of day.
why: DateOnly (and TimeOnly for times) avoid the hidden midnight that DateTime always carries.

q: The ?? operator...
choices: gives the right side when the left side is null
throws when the left is null
why: a ?? b means: a, unless a is null, then b.

q: What does this print?
why: ?. stops at null and gives null; ?? then supplies -1.

q: Assign only if the variable is still null.
why: ??= assigns the right side only when the left side is null.

q: Which is a switch EXPRESSION?
why: A switch expression uses => arms and produces a value.

q: What does this print?
why: Relational patterns are checked top to bottom; 720 fails >= 800 and matches >= 700.

q: Fill in the 'anything else' arm.
why: The discard pattern _ matches any value, like default in a switch statement.

q: What does 'and' do in: score is >= 600 and < 700
choices: Combines two patterns: both must match
why: and, or, not combine patterns.

q: A switch expression that doesn't cover every possible value gives a compiler warning.
why: Warning CS8509: the switch expression is not exhaustive.

q: GetType() == typeof(CardPayment) vs payment is CardPayment: what's the difference?
choices: 'is' also matches classes derived from CardPayment
why: GetType() == typeof(...) needs the exact type; 'is' accepts subclasses too.

q: Match a list starting with "deposit" and capture the second item.
why: List patterns: ["deposit", var amount] matches two items and captures the second.

q: Which pattern checks a property?
why: A property pattern lists properties in { } with their own patterns.

q: How do you return two values without writing a class?
choices: A tuple like (decimal Total, int Count)
why: A named tuple returns several values at once.

q: Swap two variables without a temporary one.
why: (left, right) = (right, left) builds a tuple of the old values and deconstructs it.

q: What does this print?
why: Tuple == compares element by element by position; the names don't matter.

q: JsonSerializer.Serialize(item) where item is (string Name, int Quantity) gives...
why: Tuple elements are fields, and System.Text.Json skips fields by default. Even with IncludeFields you get Item1/Item2: names exist only in source code.

q: Ignore the third value when deconstructing.
why: The discard _ throws away a value you don't need.

q: What makes a normal class usable in var (a, b) = obj;?
choices: A Deconstruct method with out parameters
why: Any type with a Deconstruct(out ..., out ...) method can be deconstructed; records get one for free.

q: Value tuples are mutable structs: you can change copy.X without changing the original.
why: ValueTuple has public fields and is copied by value.

q: Make a copy of p1 with a new name.
why: A with expression copies the record and changes only the listed properties.

q: What does this print?
why: with makes a NEW record; the original is unchanged.

q: A record has a List<string> Orders. After var copy = buyer with { Name = "Kim" }; copy.Orders.Add("Tea") ...
choices: Both buyer and copy have Tea
why: with is a SHALLOW copy: both records point at the same list.

q: Two records new Person("Anna") each with their own empty List property. Are they equal?
choices: No, the lists are compared by reference
why: Record equality compares each member; a List compares by reference, so two different lists make the records unequal.

q: What does 'sealed' on a record do?
choices: Stops other types inheriting from it
why: Inheriting from a sealed type is compile error CS0509.

q: C# 14: start an extension block for TransportationModel.
why: extension(Type name) { } blocks can add methods, properties and static members.

q: C# 14 extension blocks can add extension PROPERTIES, which the old 'this' style cannot.
why: The old style (static method with 'this' on the first parameter) only adds methods.

q: Why does a switch over every sealed subtype of an abstract record still need _ => ...?
choices: Another project could add a new subtype, so the compiler can't know the list is complete
why: Warning CS8509 without it. A future 'closed' keyword would tell the compiler the list is complete.

q: 'with' works on normal classes.
why: Compile error CS8858. It works on records, record structs, structs and anonymous types.

q: A record validates Name only in its constructor. What does valid with { Name = "" } do?
choices: Succeeds: with doesn't run the constructor's check
why: with copies the object and calls the init accessor, skipping constructor logic. Put the check in init.

q: C# 14: assign the hidden backing field inside init.
code: public string Name { get; init => ____ = value; }
why: The field keyword refers to the compiler-generated backing field.

q: Fastest way to look up a product by its code?
why: Dictionary lookups take about the same time however many items there are (O(1)); a List checks one by one.

q: Which collection never holds duplicates?
why: Add returns false when the item is already there.

q: Read a dictionary value without an exception if the key is missing.
why: TryGetValue returns false instead of throwing KeyNotFoundException.

q: What does this print?
code:
var stock = new Dictionary<string, int>();
Console.WriteLine(stock["Tea"]);
why: The indexer throws for a missing key. Use TryGetValue or GetValueOrDefault.

q: When does a LINQ Where(...) query run?
choices: When you loop over it or call ToList/Count
why: Deferred execution: a query is a recipe until something reads it.

q: First() vs Single() on a sequence with TWO matches:
choices: First returns the first; Single throws
why: Single insists on exactly one match.

q: What does this print?
why: FirstOrDefault returns default(int), which is 0, for an empty sequence.

q: Which is better to check 'is there at least one'?
why: Any() stops at the first item; Count() may walk the whole sequence.

q: Group products by category.
why: GroupBy returns groups, each with a Key and its items.

q: Total value of the stock.
why: Sum adds up the selector's results.

q: new { Category = g.Key, Value = ... } creates...
why: Anonymous types have no name you can write, so they work inside one method (with var).

q: OrderBy changes the original list.
why: LINQ returns a new sequence; List.Sort() sorts in place.

q: FrozenDictionary is best when...
choices: Built once at startup and read many times
why: Slower to build, fastest to read, can never change (5.3's benchmark measured it).

q: What does yield return do?
choices: Hands out one item and pauses until the next is asked for
why: The compiler turns the method into an enumerator that resumes after each yield.

q: What does this print?
why: Calling an iterator runs NOTHING until someone loops over it.

q: Stop an iterator early.
why: yield break ends the sequence.

q: When is the error thrown in: IEnumerable<string> Gen(int n) { ThrowIfNegative(n); ... yield return ...; } called as Gen(-1)?
why: Argument checks inside an iterator run late. Fix: check first, then return a local iterator function.

q: foreach over an iterator that reads a file, then 'break' after the first line. Is the file closed?
choices: Yes, foreach calls Dispose(), which runs the iterator's finally/using
why: foreach always disposes the enumerator, even after break.

q: The one method IEnumerable<T> requires.
why: foreach calls GetEnumerator(), then MoveNext()/Current.

q: Which two members does foreach use on an IEnumerator<T>?
why: while (cursor.MoveNext()) { var item = cursor.Current; }

q: Adding to a List<T> while looping it with foreach throws InvalidOperationException.
why: "Collection was modified; enumeration operation may not execute."

q: query.Count() then query.First() on a database query runs the query...
why: Each use re-runs the recipe. ToList() once if you need the results twice.

q: Take the first 5 items of an endless sequence.
why: Take stops asking after n items, so an endless iterator is fine.

q: A class with a public Add method that implements IEnumerable supports new Shelf { "Tea", "Coffee" }.
why: Collection initializers call Add for each item.

q: In MVC, which part handles the request and picks a view?
why: A controller action receives the request, works with models, and returns a result such as View().

q: Restrict a route value to integers.
why: Route constraints like {id:int} make /products/abc not match (404).

q: What does RedirectToAction("Index") return to the browser?
why: A redirect tells the browser to make a new GET request (Post/Redirect/Get).

q: Which survives exactly one redirect?
why: TempData is stored (cookie by default) and read once on the next request.

q: ViewBag and ViewData share the same storage.
why: ViewBag.X is just a dynamic view over ViewData["X"].

q: Check validation in a POST action.
why: ModelState.IsValid is false when binding or [Required]/[Range] checks failed.

q: Why redirect after a successful POST?
choices: So refreshing the page doesn't re-submit the form
why: Post/Redirect/Get: a refresh repeats the GET, not the POST.

q: Which attribute makes a property required in a form model?
why: Data annotations like [Required], [Range], [StringLength] drive validation.

q: RedirectToAction("Indx") (typo) on a ProductsController gives...
why: Action names are strings, checked only when the browser follows the redirect. nameof(Index) avoids this.

q: Refer to the action name safely.
why: nameof(Index) is checked by the compiler; a typo won't compile.

q: In a .cshtml file, what does @model ProductModel do?
choices: Declares the type of Model in the view
why: Model is then strongly typed in the view.

q: Razor encodes @product.Name, so <script> in a name is shown as text.
why: @ output is HTML-encoded by default; Html.Raw turns that off (dangerous).

q: A view component is best for...
choices: A reusable piece of UI with its own logic, like a sidebar
why: Unlike a partial, a view component runs its own C# to fetch data.

q: Render a view component in a view.
why: Or as a tag helper: <vc:recent-activity-sidebar />.

q: Where does View() inside a view component look for its view?
why: The view component name without the ViewComponent suffix.

q: A custom IModelBinder is for...
choices: Turning request text into a type the default binder can't parse (e.g. strict ISO dates)
why: 3.2 binds dates only in yyyy-MM-dd format.

q: A partial view can fetch its own data.
why: A partial only renders the model it's given; a view component can run code.

q: Which type receives an uploaded file in an action?
why: IFormFile gives the name, length, content type and a stream.

q: Why not trust the uploaded file's name or extension?
choices: The client chooses them; check the real file signature (magic bytes)
why: A .jpg can be anything. 3.3 checks the first bytes and saves under a new random name.

q: A form that uploads files needs this enctype.
why: Without it, the browser sends only the file name.

q: With [RequestSizeLimit] exceeded, what did 3.3's avatar parameter become?
choices: The first part of the file
why: So the action must null-check it; without the check it crashed with a 500.

q: Saving uploads under Path.GetRandomFileName() avoids overwriting and path tricks like ../.
why: Never build a path from the client's file name.

q: Which HTTP method should a form that changes data use?
why: GET must be safe to repeat (links, refresh, crawlers).

q: Model binding: an action Edit(int id, ProductForm form). Where can id come from?
choices: Route values, the query string or form fields
why: MVC looks in form fields, route values and the query string by default; [FromRoute] etc. pin one.

q: Which command turns a class library into a NuGet package?
why: dotnet pack makes a .nupkg.

q: ProjectReference vs PackageReference:
choices: ProjectReference uses source in the same solution; PackageReference uses a versioned .nupkg
why: Packages are for sharing across solutions and teams; versions matter.

q: Tell NuGet about a local folder feed (nuget.config).
why: 4.1's ConsumerApp finds the package in ../LocalNuGetFeed.

q: Version="[2.0.0]" in a PackageReference means...
why: Square brackets = exact. Version="2.0.0" alone means 2.0.0 or higher.

q: Make an extension method on string.
why: The 'this' on the first parameter makes "Hello".ToUrlSlug() possible.

q: What is a value object?
choices: Defined only by its values, immutable, e.g. Money
why: Two Money(10, "USD") are the same thing; they have no identity.

q: What is an aggregate?
choices: A cluster of objects changed only through one root that enforces the rules
why: BankAccountAggregate: you can't change the balance except through Deposit/Withdraw.

q: Domain events are named...
why: An event is a fact that already happened.

q: Why use a factory method like BankAccount.Open(...) with a private constructor?
choices: Callers can't skip the rules that Open checks
why: The only way in goes through the checks.

q: A record whose check is only in its constructor can be made invalid with 'with'.
why: 4.2's MoneyPositionalVariation: positional with { Amount = -5 } gives -5.

q: A hand-written fake repository in tests is...
choices: A small class implementing the interface with an in-memory list
why: 4.2 uses ~10-line fakes instead of Moq: anyone can read them.

q: In xUnit, which attribute marks a test with no parameters?
why: [Theory] + [InlineData] for parameterised tests.

q: Assert that code throws.
why: Assert.Throws<T> fails if nothing (or something else) is thrown.

q: Run the same test with several inputs.
why: [Theory] runs once per [InlineData].

q: AddSingleton vs AddScoped in a web app:
choices: Singleton: one for the app's life; Scoped: one per request
why: Transient = a new one every time it's asked for.

q: Playwright tests do what?
choices: Drive a real browser against the running app
why: 4.3 opens 3.1's pages in Chromium and clicks through them.

q: Wait until an element has the right text (Playwright).
why: Expect(...) assertions retry until true or timeout, unlike a one-time read.

q: Which locator style is most robust?
why: Role + accessible name survives layout changes.

q: WebApplicationFactory can start the app in the test process without a real port.
why: That's for in-memory HTTP tests; Playwright needs a real server, so 4.3 starts one.

q: PositivePositive / PositiveNegative / NegativeNegative in this repo mean...
why: Every behaviour gets all three.

q: What does await do?
choices: Frees the thread and continues later when the task finishes
why: The method pauses; the thread can do other work meanwhile.

q: What does this print?
why: count++ is read-add-write; threads overwrite each other. Use Interlocked.Increment or lock.

q: Add 1 safely from many threads.
why: An atomic read-add-write.

q: Protect a block so only one thread runs it at a time.
why: lock(gate) { } lets one thread in at a time.

q: Why copy the loop variable before starting a thread in a for loop?
choices: All lambdas share ONE for-loop variable and see its final value
why: for (int i...) has one i; foreach gives a new variable each round (since C# 5).

q: Task.WhenAll(tasks) ...
choices: Finishes when every task has finished
why: Task.WhenAny finishes at the first.

q: event vs a public delegate field:
choices: Outside code can only += / -= an event, not invoke or overwrite it
why: With a field, any caller could set it to null or fire it.

q: Call an event only if someone subscribed.
why: Finished?.Invoke(...) does nothing when there are no subscribers.

q: async void should only be used for event handlers.
why: Exceptions from async void can't be caught by the caller; return Task instead.

q: A bounded channel with FullMode = Wait makes the producer...
choices: Wait when the channel is full (backpressure)
why: That stops a fast producer from filling memory.

q: Read everything from a channel until it's completed.
why: Ends when the writer calls Complete() and the channel is empty.

q: Tell readers no more items are coming.
why: Without it, ReadAllAsync waits forever.

q: ArrayPool<byte>.Shared.Rent(4096) — what must you do after?
choices: Return(buffer) so it can be reused
why: Rent/Return reuses arrays and avoids garbage collection work.

q: When is ValueTask better than Task?
choices: When the result is often already available (no real async work)
why: It avoids allocating a Task on the fast path.

q: Benchmarks must run in...
why: Debug builds aren't optimised; the numbers would be meaningless.

q: Show allocations in a BenchmarkDotNet run.
why: Adds the Allocated column.

q: In 5.3, reading string.Length via PropertyInfo.GetValue each time was about how much slower than direct?
why: ~12 ns vs ~0.15 ns, plus 24 B allocated (boxing the int).

q: A benchmark is only fair if...
choices: Every method computes the same answer
why: 5.3's tests check all variations return the same value.

q: IAsyncEnumerable<T> is looped with...
why: Each item can arrive after an await.

q: Let WithCancellation(token) reach the async iterator.
code: async IAsyncEnumerable<int> Ticks([____] CancellationToken token = default)
why: Without it the caller's token is silently ignored (warning CS8425).

q: A streaming endpoint (returns IAsyncEnumerable) fails halfway. The client gets...
why: The 200 was already sent with the first items. Check errors before streaming.

q: EF Core AsAsyncEnumerable() vs ToListAsync():
choices: Rows handled one at a time vs all loaded into a list first
why: Memory stays flat for big tables.

q: .NET 10 has LINQ for IAsyncEnumerable built in (Where, Select, ToListAsync) without a package.
why: System.Linq.AsyncEnumerable; earlier versions needed System.Linq.Async.

q: What does this print?
why: Like normal iterators, nothing runs until something loops over it.

q: The N+1 query problem is...
choices: Loading a list (1 query) then each item's related data (N more queries)
why: 6.1 logs the SQL: lazy loading in a loop sends one query per book.

q: Load each book's author in the same query.
why: Include adds a JOIN; ThenInclude goes one level deeper.

q: Load the author's profile too.
why: ThenInclude continues from the previous Include.

q: AsNoTracking() is good for...
choices: Read-only queries: faster, EF doesn't watch the objects
why: Tracked objects cost memory and time; a list page doesn't need them.

q: Two SaveChanges calls that must both succeed or both fail need...
why: One SaveChanges is already one transaction; several need an explicit one.

q: Start an explicit transaction.
code: await using var transaction = await database.Database.____();
why: Commit with CommitAsync; disposing without commit rolls back.

q: TransactionScope with EF Core on SQLite...
choices: Throws: SQLite doesn't support ambient transactions
why: 6.2 found EF refuses (AmbientTransactionWarning as an error).

q: A soft delete...
choices: Marks the row deleted (IsDeleted) and hides it with a query filter
why: The data stays for audits/undo; HasQueryFilter hides it.

q: IOptions vs IOptionsSnapshot vs IOptionsMonitor: which sees settings changes while the app runs, even in a singleton?
why: IOptions reads once; Snapshot once per request (scoped); Monitor always current.

q: A cache stampede is...
choices: Many requests missing the cache at once and all hitting the database
why: HybridCache (6.3) lets only one caller rebuild the value.

q: Session data in ASP.NET Core is stored...
choices: On the server, found by an id in a cookie
why: 6.4 stores the cart as JSON in session.

q: Enable sessions in Program.cs (middleware).
why: Plus builder.Services.AddSession() and a distributed cache.

q: Which handles every unhandled exception centrally in ASP.NET Core 8+?
why: One place turns exceptions into ProblemDetails responses.

q: ProblemDetails is...
choices: A standard JSON shape for HTTP errors (type, title, status, detail)
why: Content-Type application/problem+json (RFC 9457).

q: Showing stack traces to users in Production is fine.
why: They leak internals; show a friendly page and log the details.

q: FromSql($"SELECT * FROM Products WHERE Name = {name}") is safe because...
choices: The interpolated value becomes a SQL parameter
why: FromSqlRaw with string concatenation would be injectable.

q: ExecuteUpdateAsync(...) does what?
choices: Sends one UPDATE statement without loading rows
why: Bulk update in one statement; tracked objects aren't updated.

q: A concurrency token makes SaveChanges throw when...
choices: Someone else changed the row since you loaded it
why: DbUpdateConcurrencyException instead of last-write-wins.

q: Delete all discontinued products in one statement.
why: One DELETE; no objects loaded.

q: IEntityTypeConfiguration<T> is for...
choices: Putting one entity's database setup in its own class
why: Applied with modelBuilder.ApplyConfiguration(new ProductConfiguration()).

q: Apply every configuration class in the assembly.
why: No list to maintain, but it applies configurations meant for other contexts too.

q: Table-per-hierarchy means...
choices: All subclasses in ONE table with a discriminator column
why: HasDiscriminator<string>("Type").HasValue<Material>("Material")...

q: OfType<MaterialModel>() on a table-per-hierarchy set becomes...
why: With table-per-type it would be a JOIN instead.

q: A shadow property is...
choices: A column EF maps that the C# class doesn't have
why: builder.Property<int>("Id") + HasKey("Id").

q: EF.Property<int>(invoice, "Id") on an already-loaded object...
choices: Throws: it only works inside a LINQ query
why: Use database.Entry(invoice).Property<int>("Id").CurrentValue instead.

q: Always load the lines with every invoice.
why: Turn it off for one query with IgnoreAutoIncludes().

q: IgnoreAutoIncludes() alone, after the same DbContext already loaded Acme's lines, returns Acme with...
why: Tracked objects get attached to each other. Add AsNoTracking() for a list page.

q: Why expose a private list as linesCollection.AsReadOnly() instead of IEnumerable?
choices: IEnumerable over the List can be cast back to List<T> and changed
why: AsReadOnly throws NotSupportedException on Add and can't be cast back.

q: With no Invoices DbSet, what did EF name the invoice table?
why: Table names come from DbSet property names; otherwise the class name. Use ToTable("Invoices").

q: OfType + Join + GroupBy with a Sum can run as ONE SQL command.
why: 6.7's report: WHERE Type='Material', INNER JOIN, GROUP BY with SUM.

q: Which file wraps every view in the same header and footer?
why: @RenderBody() in _Layout marks where each view goes.

q: In _Layout.cshtml, mark where each view's content goes.
why: RenderBody inserts the current view.

q: _ViewImports.cshtml is for...
choices: @using and @addTagHelper lines shared by all views
why: Saves repeating the same usings in every view.

q: Throw the domain's own exception when money runs out.
why: A custom exception carries the details (balance, requested amount).

q: Why does the domain library (Banking.Domain) have no database or web code?
choices: So the business rules can be tested and reused without infrastructure
why: The repository interface says WHAT it needs; other projects say HOW.

q: A loose .dll reference (<Reference HintPath>) brings its dependencies along automatically.
why: Only packages carry dependency information; that's why 4.1 says avoid loose dlls.

q: Where does a .csproj put package metadata like the id and version?
why: dotnet pack reads them from the project file.

q: Authentication vs authorization:
choices: Who are you? vs What may you do?
why: UseAuthentication must come before UseAuthorization.

q: Only admins may call this action.
why: Roles = "Admin,Manager" means EITHER role; stacking two [Authorize] means BOTH.

q: [Authorize(Roles = "Admin")] when a logged-in non-admin calls it returns...
why: 401 means not logged in; 403 means logged in but not allowed.

q: Two separate [Authorize(Roles = ...)] attributes on one action mean...
why: Each attribute must pass.

q: XSS (cross-site scripting) is...
choices: Injecting script that runs in other users' browsers
why: Razor's @ encoding stops it; Html.Raw on user input brings it back.

q: CSRF is stopped by...
choices: An antiforgery token in each form, checked on POST
why: [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] / automatic in Razor forms.

q: Check the antiforgery token on a POST action.
why: Forms built with tag helpers include the token automatically.

q: 7.2's antiforgery cookie had SecurePolicy Always. Over plain HTTP the POST...
choices: Crashed: the cookie can't be sent without HTTPS
why: The tests had to use HTTPS.

q: A Content-Security-Policy header can block inline scripts even if XSS gets in.
why: Defence in depth: encoding first, CSP second.

q: Which base class runs a long-lived loop in the background of a web app?
why: Override ExecuteAsync(stoppingToken); register with AddHostedService<T>().

q: Register a background service.
why: It starts with the app and is stopped on shutdown.

q: A BackgroundService needs a scoped service (DbContext). It should...
choices: Create a scope with IServiceScopeFactory for each unit of work
why: A singleton holding a scoped service is a captive dependency.

q: PeriodicTimer vs Task.Delay in a loop:
choices: PeriodicTimer ticks on a fixed schedule; Delay adds the work time to each gap
why: 7.3's TimerStyle variation shows the drift.

q: Output caching stores...
choices: Whole HTTP responses on the server
why: [OutputCache] / CacheOutput(); VaryByQuery for different query strings.

q: Add a health check endpoint.
why: Plus builder.Services.AddHealthChecks().

q: ResponseCache vs OutputCache:
choices: ResponseCache only sets headers for browsers/proxies; OutputCache stores responses on the server
why: 7.4 compares them in its variations.

q: A percentage rollout should use...
choices: A stable hash of the user id, so a user stays in or out
why: Random flickers between requests (7.5's variation showed it).

q: Where must GitHub Actions workflow files live?
why: GitHub only runs YAML files from .github/workflows/.

q: concurrency: cancel-in-progress: true does what?
choices: A newer push cancels the older, still-running run
why: That's why this repo's history shows 'cancelled' runs that aren't failures.

q: An idempotent migration script...
choices: Can be run again safely: each migration checks if it was already applied
why: dotnet ef migrations script --idempotent wraps each in IF NOT EXISTS.

q: Generate a script safe to run twice.
why: Ideal for deployment pipelines.

q: Expand-then-contract for zero downtime means...
choices: Add new things first (both versions work), remove old things in a later release
why: Old and new app versions run side by side during a deploy.

q: Why wrap CREATE PROCEDURE in EXEC(N'...') inside the idempotent script?
choices: CREATE PROCEDURE must be first in a batch; it can't sit inside an IF block directly
why: 7.7 hit this error.

q: app.UseWebSockets() + context.WebSockets.AcceptWebSocketAsync() gives...
choices: A two-way connection both sides can send on any time
why: Raw frames; SignalR (8.8) builds on top with reconnects and groups.

q: One ReceiveAsync call returns...
choices: Part of a message: loop until EndOfMessage
why: Big messages arrive in several frames.

q: IDistributedCache with Redis is for...
choices: A cache shared by every server instance
why: In-memory caches differ per server.

q: After updating a price in the database, the cache should...
why: No invalidation = stale prices until expiry (7.9's variation).

q: IDistributedCache stores byte arrays (GetString/SetString are helpers on top).
why: You serialize objects yourself, e.g. to JSON.

q: A minimal API GET endpoint.
why: MapPost, MapPut, MapDelete for the others.

q: Why return Results<Ok<Book>, NotFound> instead of IResult?
choices: OpenAPI can see both possible status codes
why: With plain IResult the document loses the 404.

q: A minimal API parameter bool uppercase with no default and no ?uppercase in the URL gives...
why: Non-nullable without a default = required. Use bool uppercase = false.

q: Why use a DTO (SaveBookRequestModel) instead of binding the entity?
choices: Clients can't over-post fields like CostPrice, and secret fields don't leak in responses
why: 8.1's entity endpoint let a client set costPrice: -100.

q: A JWT is...
choices: A signed token carrying claims; the server checks the signature
why: Anyone can READ a JWT; only the key holder can SIGN one.

q: Require a policy on an endpoint.
why: Policies are defined with AddAuthorizationBuilder().AddPolicy(...).

q: ClockSkew in JWT validation is...
choices: Extra time allowed after expiry (default 5 minutes)
why: Set to TimeSpan.Zero for tests that expect exact expiry.

q: Why use IHttpClientFactory instead of new HttpClient() per call?
choices: Avoids socket exhaustion and DNS problems; adds named/typed clients
why: It pools the underlying handlers.

q: Add retries, timeouts and a circuit breaker in one call.
why: From Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience.

q: A circuit breaker...
choices: Stops calling a failing service for a while, failing fast
why: Gives the other service time to recover.

q: A token bucket limiter...
choices: Allows a fixed number per minute exactly
Refills tokens over time and allows short bursts
why: Fixed window, sliding window, token bucket and concurrency are the four built-ins.

q: Apply a rate-limit policy to an endpoint.
why: Plus app.UseRateLimiter().

q: Default status code when a request is rate-limited (ASP.NET Core)?
why: Set options.RejectionStatusCode = 429 to send Too Many Requests.

q: Native AOT publishing breaks code that...
choices: Relies on runtime reflection (e.g. reflection-based JSON)
why: Use source-generated JsonSerializerContext instead.

q: Trimming removes...
choices: Code that looks unused, which can break reflection
why: Mark risky code with [RequiresUnreferencedCode].

q: dotnet publish --self-contained includes...
choices: The .NET runtime too, so the machine doesn't need .NET installed
why: Bigger output, no install needed.

q: In Razor Pages, the code for Contacts.cshtml lives in...
why: OnGet / OnPost handlers instead of actions.

q: Bind a property for POST in a PageModel.
code:
[____]
public ContactForm Form { get; set; } = new();
why: Add SupportsGet = true to bind on GET too.

q: Blazor Server runs component code...
choices: On the server, with UI updates over a SignalR connection
why: Blazor WebAssembly runs it in the browser instead (this repo's Playground).

q: Two-way bind an input in Blazor.
why: @bind:event="oninput" updates on every keystroke.

q: EventCallback vs Action for a component parameter:
choices: EventCallback re-renders the parent automatically and supports async
why: Prefer EventCallback for child-to-parent events.

q: A strongly typed SignalR hub (Hub<IChatClient>) prevents...
why: With Clients.All.SendAsync("ReceiveMesage") a typo just silently does nothing.

q: Clients.Others sends to...
why: Clients.Caller = only the sender; Clients.Group(name) = a group.

q: gRPC defines its API in...
choices: A .proto file; code is generated for both sides
why: Field numbers in .proto must never be reused.

q: A gRPC deadline that passes gives the client...
why: Deadlines travel to the server, which can stop early.

q: gRPC needs HTTP/2.
why: That's also why browsers need gRPC-Web.

q: Overload + for Money.
code: public static Money ____ +(Money left, Money right)
why: Operators are public static methods named operator +, operator ==, ...

q: Why is Money's conversion to decimal 'explicit' rather than 'implicit'?
choices: Converting loses the currency, so the caller must ask for it with a cast
why: Implicit conversions happen silently.

q: Expression<Func<T, bool>> vs Func<T, bool>:
choices: An Expression is code as data that can be read (e.g. turned into SQL) or compiled
why: EF Core reads expressions to build SQL.

q: Comparison<T> is used by...
why: A Func<T, T, int> with the same body must be wrapped: new Comparison<T>(func).

q: Declare a custom GENERIC delegate.
why: Same shape as Func<T, TResult>, but with its own name.

q: Later configuration sources...
choices: override earlier ones for the same key
why: appsettings.json < appsettings.{Env}.json < environment variables < command line.

q: A YAML list in a later file with FEWER items than an earlier file's list...
choices: Overwrites by index; extra old items stay
why: Configuration merges lists by index (9.2 found this).

q: A fluent builder returns ___ from each method so calls chain.
why: new OrderBuilder().ForCustomer("Ann").AddLine(...).Build()

q: 'required' on a property means...
choices: It can't be null at run time
The object initializer must set it, or it doesn't compile
why: C# 11. Together with init, it's set once at creation.

q: The Strategy pattern...
choices: Swaps one algorithm for another behind the same interface
why: Shipping cost strategies: standard, express, free.

q: The State pattern replaces...
choices: A big switch on status with one class per state that knows its allowed moves
why: pending -> paid -> shipped -> delivered.

q: A mediator...
choices: Lets senders send a request without knowing which handler handles it
why: mediator.Send(new PlaceOrderRequest(...)).

q: The Command pattern is good for...
choices: Undo/redo: each action is an object that can be executed and undone
why: 9.4's editor keeps a history of commands.

q: Chain of responsibility:
choices: Each handler handles the request or passes it to the next
why: Approval limits: team lead, manager, director.

q: A decorator...
choices: Wraps an object with the same interface to add behaviour (logging, caching)
why: Callers can't tell the difference.

q: DispatchProxy is used for...
choices: Intercepting every call on an interface at run time (AOP logging)
why: Rethrow with ExceptionDispatchInfo to keep the original stack trace.

q: In TPL Dataflow, a BatchBlock<T>(100)...
why: Then an ActionBlock saves each batch.

q: Let completion flow from one block to the next.
why: Without it the last block never completes.

q: Compensation in a workflow (saga) means...
choices: Undoing earlier steps when a later step fails
why: Refund the payment if shipping fails.

q: Rx Throttle (debounce) vs Sample:
choices: Throttle waits for a quiet period; Sample takes the latest every interval
why: 9.8's price ticks show the difference.

q: IObservable<T> vs IEnumerable<T>:
choices: Observable PUSHES items to you; Enumerable lets you PULL them
why: Subscribe vs foreach.

q: Register a service with one instance per request.
why: AddSingleton = one forever; AddTransient = new each time.

q: GetService<T>() vs GetRequiredService<T>() when T isn't registered:
why: Required is the usual choice.

q: A singleton that takes a scoped service in its constructor is called...
why: ValidateScopes/ValidateOnBuild catch it at startup.

q: Register several IJob implementations without duplicates.
why: Adds only if that exact implementation isn't registered yet.

q: Prefixes: Add... / Use... / Map... mean...
choices: register services / add middleware / add endpoints
why: AddControllers, UseRouting, MapGet.

q: Reflection: PropertyInfo.SetValue on an 'init' property...
choices: Works: reflection skips the compiler's init rule
why: 9.9's ReflectionVariation test proves it.

q: An exception thrown inside a method called with MethodInfo.Invoke arrives as...
why: Look at InnerException.

q: In a SaaS app, a tenant is...
choices: One customer company using the app
why: Many tenants share one app (and here, one database).

q: A global query filter...
choices: Adds a WHERE to every query for that entity automatically
why: HasQueryFilter(p => p.TenantId == CurrentTenantId).

q: Add the tenant filter.
why: Every query gets WHERE TenantId = ... without anyone writing it.

q: Why must the filter read a PROPERTY of the DbContext, not a local variable from OnModelCreating?
choices: The model is built once and cached; a local is baked in for the first tenant forever
why: 10.1's CapturedFilter variation: globex saw acme's rows.

q: TenantContext is registered as...
why: A singleton would let requests overwrite each other's tenant.

q: Acme asks for globex's project id. The API should return...
why: 404 doesn't reveal that the id exists.

q: FromSql($"SELECT * FROM Projects") is still filtered by the tenant query filter.
why: EF wraps the raw query and adds the filter.

q: Database.ExecuteSqlAsync("UPDATE Projects ...") is filtered by the tenant query filter.
why: Raw commands bypass the filter: add WHERE TenantId = {tenant} yourself.

q: Admin-only: turn the filter off for one query.
why: Keep these rare and behind an admin policy.

q: Why is the X-Tenant header alone unsafe in production?
choices: The client chooses it; take the tenant from the signed token or check membership
why: Anyone could type 'globex'.

q: When no tenant is set, the filter compares with "" so the query returns...
why: A forgotten tenant sees nothing, not everyone's data.

q: Database per tenant vs shared database with TenantId:
choices: Per tenant: strongest isolation but N databases to migrate; shared: cheap but one bug can leak
why: Many SaaS apps mix them.

q: SaveChanges stamps TenantId on Added rows. What happens if code changes an existing row's TenantId?
why: Moving data between tenants is blocked.

q: Read the tenant from the subdomain acme.myapp.com.
why: 10.1's FromHost also rejects www, the bare domain and nested subdomains.

q: Scoped services in conventional middleware should be injected...
why: The middleware instance lives for the whole app.

q: A tenantId sent in the JSON body is ignored because the request model has no such field.
why: The client can't choose where data goes.

q: Most important SaaS test?
choices: Tenant A can't read, change or delete tenant B's data
why: A cross-tenant leak is the classic SaaS disaster.

q: Indexing TenantId matters because...
why: Without it, each request scans the whole table as tenants grow.

q: Many tenants can share one app and one database.
why: That's the shared model 10.1 uses.

q: Which SaaS building block usually comes AFTER multi-tenancy?
why: Then plans/limits, billing webhooks, audit log, outbox, observability.

q: Fill in the operator so a missing tenant becomes "".
why: Null-coalescing: a forgotten tenant matches no rows.

q: The claim-based tenant source is safest because...
choices: Changing a signed token's claim breaks its signature
why: Header/subdomain/path are all chosen by the client.

q: What does this print?
why: int / int is integer division: the fraction is dropped.

q: What does this print?
why: One double operand makes it double division.

q: What does this print?
why: Math.Round uses banker's rounding by default: to the nearest EVEN number. Use MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero for 3.

q: Round 2.5 to 3, the way people expect.
why: The default (ToEven) gives 2.

q: What does this print?
why: Strings are immutable: ToUpper returns a NEW string that was thrown away.

q: Building a string in a loop of 10,000 items is best done with...
why: += makes a new string every time; StringBuilder appends in place.

q: String interpolation.
why: A $ before the string enables {expressions}.

q: What does this print?
why: Type pattern + when guard; arms are checked in order.

q: What does this print?
code:
int? maybe = null;
Console.WriteLine(maybe is null ? "none" : "some");
why: is null is the safe null test (== can be overloaded).

q: 'is not null' vs '!= null':
choices: 'is not null' can't be changed by an overloaded != operator
why: Patterns ignore operator overloads.

q: What does this print?
why: Deferred execution: the query runs when Join reads it, after Add.

q: What does this print?
why: ToList() ran the query before the Add.

q: What does this print?
Keep only products that are out of stock.
why: Where filters; Select reshapes.

q: Turn each product into its name.
why: Select maps each item to something new.

q: Sort by category, then by name.
why: A second OrderBy would replace the first sort.

q: Distinct() vs new HashSet<T>(items):
choices: Same unique items; HashSet also gives fast Contains afterwards
why: 2.1's CollectionType variation compares them.

q: What does this print?
why: tea and coffee.

q: Join(...) in LINQ needs...
choices: Two key selectors (outer and inner) and a result selector
why: outer.Join(inner, o => o.Key, i => i.Key, (o, i) => ...).

q: IReadOnlyList<T> stops the CALLER from adding items, but the owner can still change the list.
why: It's a read-only view, not an immutable copy (use ImmutableList for that).

q: What does this print?
why: yield break ends the sequence; 3 is never produced (compiler warns about unreachable code).

q: TempData is removed after it's read once.
why: Unless you call Keep or Peek.

q: Return a 404 from an MVC action.
why: Also Ok(), BadRequest(), View(), RedirectToAction().

q: [HttpPost] public IActionResult Create(ProductForm form) — where do form's values come from?
choices: Model binding from the posted form fields
why: Field names must match property names.

q: Encapsulation means...
choices: Keeping data private and changing it only through methods that enforce rules
why: Balance { get; private set; } + Deposit/Withdraw.

q: Interface vs abstract class:
choices: An interface is a contract only; an abstract class can share code and state
why: A class can implement many interfaces but inherit one class.

q: A property anyone can read but only the class can set.
why: Changes must go through methods.

q: What does this print?
why: Records compare by value.

q: Two class instances with the same values are == by default.
why: Classes compare by reference unless you override Equals/==.

q: Why test behaviour through the public API instead of private methods?
choices: Tests then survive refactoring inside the class
why: Private details can change; behaviour shouldn't.

q: What does this print?
why: Calling it starts it; it isn't done until the delay finishes.

q: .Result or .Wait() on a task in UI or old ASP.NET code can...
choices: Deadlock: the thread waits for work that needs that same thread
why: Use await all the way.

q: Cancel after 3 seconds.
why: Pass cancel.Token to the async methods.

q: Task.Run is for...
choices: Moving CPU-heavy work off the current thread
why: I/O is already async; wrapping it in Task.Run just wastes a thread.

q: ConfigureAwait(false) in library code means...
choices: Don't come back to the original context after the await
why: Avoids context switches; not needed in ASP.NET Core apps.

q: Span<T> can't be used across an await.
why: A Span lives on the stack; use Memory<T> across awaits.

q: Lazy loading means...
choices: Related data loads the first time you touch the property (an extra query)
why: Convenient, but a loop over it causes N+1.

q: Print EF's SQL to the console.
why: Filter with DbLoggerCategory.Database.Command for just the SQL.

q: Without a transaction, a crash between two SaveChanges calls leaves...
choices: The first saved, the second not (half an order)
why: That's why checkout uses one transaction.

q: Which environment name turns on the developer exception page by default?
why: Set by ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT (launchSettings.json does it locally).

q: Check the environment in Program.cs.
why: Also IsProduction(), IsStaging(), IsEnvironment("X").

q: Feature flags let you...
choices: Turn a feature on or off without deploying
why: Microsoft.FeatureManagement reads them from configuration.

q: AddValidation() in .NET 10 minimal APIs...
choices: Checks [Required]/[Range] on parameters automatically before the handler runs
why: Invalid input gets a 400 ProblemDetails.

q: Group endpoints under one prefix.
why: Then books.MapGet("/{id}", ...).

q: Razor Pages handler for a POST is named...
why: OnGet for GET; named handlers like OnPostDelete too.

q: What does this print?
why: twice(5) = 10, then + 1.

q: What does this print?
why: One i shared by the whole for loop; every lambda sees its final value 3.

q: What does this print?
why: foreach makes a new variable each round (since C# 5).

q: A lambda that squares a number.
code: Func<int, int> square = x ____ x * x;
why: Parameters => body.

q: Action<T> vs Func<T, TResult> vs Predicate<T>:
choices: no return / returns TResult / returns bool
returns bool / no return / returns T
why: Predicate<T> is like Func<T, bool>.

q: Where should the tenant come from for an API call with a JWT?
why: Signed, so the client can't change it.

q: ExecuteDelete is filtered by the global tenant query filter.
why: Tested in 10.1: acme deleting globex's id removed 0 rows.

q: Why does SaveChanges overwrite TenantId on new rows instead of trusting it?
choices: Code or clients could set the wrong tenant; the server decides
why: Writes are stamped with the current tenant.

q: What does this print?
why: The global filter adds WHERE TenantId = 'acme'.

q: Register the per-request tenant holder.
why: One per request.

q: A schema per tenant (acme.Projects, globex.Projects) is...
choices: The same as a shared table
In between: stronger separation than a TenantId column, cheaper than a database each
why: Migrations run once per schema.
